steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Ermi Ermi, if you read me, please respond.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Ermi...? It's not working?

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: Young Djall, could you please unbind my hands? I promise I won't run. At least let me have a smoke?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No can do! I'm not letting you go until I get you back to the Furnace.

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: I told you, you've got the wrong guy. I've been meaning to drop by the Furnace, but I really didn't escape from the thing.

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: I have a Columbian ID in my shirt pocket. I could show you right now—if you unbind my hands.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It's a long trip from Columbia to Kazdel, isn't it?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: If you'd told me you were from Rim Billiton, I probably would've believed you.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Ermi, can you hear me? Hey? Hello...?

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: The box's comm Arts structure has been ruined. You can slap it all you want, but that isn't going to fix it.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: How dare you?! It's your fault my box got crushed in the first place!

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: If I fix your little box thing for you, will you free my hands?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Can you really fix it?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Don't you pull any tricks or anything! I-I have my own methods to deal with you!

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: I got it, little Djall. Relax. I'm not going anywhere.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Hold on. Are you actually buying this, Nymph? The guy gets possessed by a re—by the ancestors and you're ready to unbind him?

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: You sure love getting your word in, kiddo, but you don't seem to know a thing about revenants or Djaj. Djaj are the only ones that can't be influenced by revenants.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I'll free just one of your hands... Hey! How'd you break yourself out of that? You tricked me!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I knew you were up to no good!

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: I hope you can appreciate how much it hurts to have my hands bound for so long.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It hurts, even though you've got iron skin?

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: It's not iron. It's tin. And it doesn't exactly hurt. It's just...
Between his metallic fingers is a single cigarette; it seems to have appeared out of nowhere.
The odd man takes it to his mouth, takes a puff, then spins the cigarette around between his fingers before carefully smothering every spark of flame in his palms.

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: Huff—Ah, that's good.

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: You can't buy cigarettes this nice in Kazdel. I have to ration them.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Hey, you promised you'd fix my box.

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: I lied.

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: A Lich created the Arts in that box, and those prideful bastards never think about repairability when they design things. That's not to say none of them earned their pride, though.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Come on, you're just going back on your word!

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: Let me finish. You're looking for someone, aren't you? I can't fix the box, but I can help you find the Lich who made it.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: H-How come you know who I'm looking for?

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: I don't, but I think I don't need to.
The strange man leans back as a puff of gray-whitish smoke gradually floats from his mouth.
The smoke disperses into a rippling cloud, like a stone being thrown into a pool of stagnant water. The revenant's trace fluctuations sweep across the area, drowning all of Kazdel in silence.
A brief moment later, the noise has reemerged, and the puff of smoke has completely dispersed.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Who are you exactly?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Just... who are you, mister?

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: They call me the Tin Man.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Tin Man...?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Look, the one you're looking for is here.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: One can count all the revenants that walk the lands on one hand. Who might you be?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: He says he's the Tin Man.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: He says he's from Columbia.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: ...Kazdel is not ready for your return yet.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Hard to blame you. I never thought I'd ever come back here when I left.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: What did you come back for?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: He says he wants to go to the Furnace.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Nymphy!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Okay okay. I won't interrupt again. Go ahead and ask.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Then allow me to... Never mind. I suppose there's nothing else to ask.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Normally, a guest of your pedigree would be received by my master, but...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Your master? That stubborn old man? Let's not tell him, save my vacation from going completely down the drain.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: If you'd like to visit and take a look beneath the Soul Furnace, I could bring you there, without telling anyone.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: (Shakes head) Not beneath it. I want to go inside it.

spans.text: (Shakes head) Not beneath it. I want to go

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Who do you want to visit there?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Who else?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Nymphy, have you gathered all the revenant fragments yet?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: They're all inside my box. Here!
The young Lich nods and nonchalantly throws the slightly misshapen box into the shadows behind her.
Her gaze shifts back and forth between the Djall and the revenant, then finally lands on the Soul Furnace that stands in the distance.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Then let's go.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Nymphy, I'll find another time to give you your reward. And here's the surprise I promised you—Do you want to go into the Soul Furnace for a walk?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Can I really?!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Can I bring friends?! So many kind people have helped us along the way! I could never have collected all the fragments so quickly without them!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Ahem, to tell the truth, I've always wanted to go inside, ever since I was a kid, just to see how it works.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Well... As it stands, we've already broken multiple rules today. so...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Give me just a minute! I'll gather everybody up!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Everybody? Hold on...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Right, for my reward, can I get some scrap Oriron...? Pohl, help me explain it to Ermi, okay?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Uh, alright.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Ah, youth. So motivated. Already sprang away like an arrow from the bow.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I never introduced myself. I'm from down below, the slums, as people call it.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: They call me the Consultant there, and I speak for them. Mr. Tin Man, and the Lich lady. Please, call me Pohl.

spans.text: there, and I speak for them. Mr. Tin Man, and the Lich lady. Please, call me Pohl.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Don't call me a lady. Don't you think that's very improper?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Oh, kiddo... In certain ways, you're still far too young.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: One, two, three, four... and me. Five! All of us are here!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Nymphy, the Furnace is a dangerous place. Why did you bring this many people? And that little girl behind you...

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: One child ticket, please.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: This is not a sightseeing spot, and we don't sell tickets! No children, either!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Sorry, Cherie. I tried my best... Maybe next time?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: There's no next time!

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: It's okay, Nymph. I was thinking that maybe the big furnace is full of flatbread like the little one we have. Turns out, it's all dark and dirty and lame!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: What flatbread? We never bake anything with the furnace nodes! Your grandpa is still waiting outside, right? Quick, go find him!

spans.text: bake anything with the furnace nodes! Your grandpa is still waiting outside, right? Quick, go find him!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: There are still so many people here. Now what am I going to do with them?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: They all helped me, a lot, and you promised me just now! They won't give you any trouble at all!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Everyone, I need all of you to give me your own words, not just Nymphy's.

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: It doesn't matter to me. All I want is to take a look at the work of that legendary designer. I've heard her signature is on the Soul Furnace's blueprints, too. Is that true?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Since when has the Soul Furnace had blueprints?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You can look all you want, but no touching. What about you, Gargoyle? What are you looking at?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: If there's a wide enough pipeline that leads straight out of the city...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Gargoyles tend to be into complicated constructions like this. Don't worry. She's just checking whether the pipelines are sturdy enough.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Right. I'm trying to see if we can crawl through them.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: What about you, Consultant? Trying to live your childhood dream? Like you said before?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (Shrugs) Is that not good enough of a reason?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I didn't expect to see you here, Qalaiša. What is a Nachzehrer who left her tribe doing here?

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: Left my tribe? No, we just hold different ideals.

spans.text: my tribe? No, we just hold different ideals.

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: As for what I am doing here... Hm, mainly, I couldn't bring myself to refuse such a sincere invitation from this cutie pie.

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: And if I manage to learn a few extraordinary witchcraft rituals while inside the Soul Furnace, that's all the better.

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: None of us here have any reason to lie. What's more, it was a Djall who invited all of us.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I've finished a whole cigarette already. Are you done with the roll call yet? I don't suppose anyone's going against their word?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Lich girl, try not to pick up your master's bad habits. Liches used to have a pretty great reputation, but now...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I'm not very well-versed in history, but I can tell you are making things up.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Okay, now. If everyone's ready, let's get going. Stay close. Don't fall behind.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Hooray! You're the best, Ermi! I knew you would be more amenable than those old, stuck-up fossils!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Turn right at the next corner.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: There are potholes on the ground three steps ahead. Keep left.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You can open your eyes now. We're here.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: So this is what it looks like inside! What's that faintly glowing thing?

spans.text: is what it looks like inside! What's that faintly glowing thing?

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: The witchcraft core.

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: This is the deepest part of the Soul Furnace. As far as I know, ever since it was built, only Liches have come here to hold rituals to appease the revenants.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: And the last ritual caused the big fireworks that led all of us here. Anything else to share?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Mr. Tin Man, should we proceed as we discussed?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Sure. I'll keep an eye out for you.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: The fireworks were only an accident, and the ceremony wasn't completed.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: My master tasked me with finding the revenant fragments scattered all over Kazdel, and I entrusted this mission to Nymph. Nymph then got your help. Which means...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: My master owes all of you a favor. No, he owes all of us a favor.

spans.text: My master owes all of you a favor. No, he owes all of

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: As the keeper of the Temple of Knowledge, a favor of his is most valuable indeed. You could accomplish quite a lot with it.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: But, as his student, I've already decided in his place to use this favor to do something exceedingly difficult.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I'm kinda getting the feeling you're about to say something horrible... Is it okay if I leave now?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No way! I invited you here. If anyone's leaving, I'm leaving first!

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Ahem, it's actually nothing to be scared of. She's just being sulky that she got taught a lesson by the stubborn old man, and she's trying to win back some face.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: What face?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: The revenant's... face. I'll finish my master's appeasement ceremony without a flaw. So, are you in?

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: Yaaahhh!

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: Sorry, I couldn't stand that awkward silence, so I thought I'd make some noise.

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: Uh, like I said, I'm just here to admire that legendary designer's work... Since I've now seen it, I'll leave this revenant business to the rest of you.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: We kept our eyes closed the whole time, and you're telling me you're already done?!

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: If it was just watching the ceremony, I'd be totally fine, but the Lich here seems to want us to be active participants?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: If we're dealing with revenants, should we let Amiya know? And the Babel members, too?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: All of us have seen how powerful the revenants can be. Even little fragments were causing chaos all over Kazdel.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Pohl, stop sweating! It's not that bad!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Not that bad? Think about it, Nymph. If it'd taken us just a little longer to get to any one of the fragments, what do you think would have happened?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: There would've been bloodshed if those gangs had drawn their blades, and that berserk colossus wouldn't have stopped its fist...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: And think about the risks when facing the revenants who have been burning in the Furnace for centuries. Is that really something we can take by ourselves?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Like I said, I'll keep an eye out for you.

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: A revenant. A powerful revenant who turned his back on his homeland, only to return as if nothing had happened.

steps.name: Qalaiša
steps.text: I have no qualms with this.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I'm fine with it, too! What's there to be scared of if we have such a bad-ass ancestor looking after us?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You're getting ahead of yourself, Nymph. Even with Mr. Tin Man here, it's not going to be easy to appease the ancestors with just the few of us.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Why do you think it'll be hard? We've met so many people on our way here. Everyone may live pretty hard lives, but we're all living life to the fullest.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Maybe the ceremony failed last time because the ancestors had heard enough nagging. I mean, when all you ever hear is the future and sacrifice, blahblahblah, how is anyone supposed to cheer up?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: If we tell them about how people in Kazdel live these days, that might drive up their enthusiasm!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Besides, the revenants might still remember that legendary designer, they might know her true identity...

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: That sounds splendid. Count me in!

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: We've made it this far. We can't go back empty-handed. And if the revenants can show us a secret passageway out of the city...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Then you're in, too! Pohl, what do you say? Still hesitating?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It's a bit of a risk, but I can't think of a reason to not go for it. I'm in.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Okay, then let's throw the ancestors an appeasement ceremony like they've never seen! What do you think, Mr. Tin Man?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I'm intrigued. I said yes to the Lich girl there because she said basically what you just did.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Huh? Really, Ermi?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: We're the ones who will walk the path of Kazdel's future, not them, so...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Of course, we have the right to do this.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Now cover your ears. I'll begin the incantations.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Let's try again. Relax... Flawed souls, come near, and heed my call.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: In the flames... as your bloodlines melt away... heed my call.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: What's going on? There's no response at all.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Mr. Tin Man, are you still there?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Maybe I've gone too deep... I'm not getting any response. Did I do something wrong?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: No, if I turn back now, I'll be admitting to a failure before it's even over.
In the shapeless shadows, spots of cold light revolve around my consciousness, leaving layered trails behind them.
Once you try to understand the logic within, you will immediately lose yourself in it. Stop. Think, think...
These... are the revenants' fragments. I remember now. I try bringing them together, but they keep escaping through my fingers, like stardust.
They are talking. There's one... two. A lot of voices slowly drawing near me. The coldness fades away, and the frigid ice burns bright. I can feel it—
Agitation, hatred, chaos... It's more than them not hearing my cries, they... are simply ignoring me. Ultimately, they are annoyed.
They want to... tear me apart.

steps.name: Quiet Voice
steps.text: Step back... Three, two, one. Cut your senses off and step back!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Ermi, are you okay?! You were standing there, shaking. That was scary!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I... I'm alright. Where is Mr. Tin Man?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: He's over there by the wall. He hasn't moved for a while now with his head down, and I'm not sure what's going on with him, or if those metallic joints ever ache.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: The ceremony... did it work?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I was returning the fragments to the revenants, but I almost lost myself in their consciousness. It was the Tin Man who saved me.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Not a big deal. I just offered a hand. You could've handled it by yourself, although it would have taken more time.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: He was standing still the whole time, why this sound feels like it's echoing inside my head?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: It's not a bad thing for kids to have that kind of drive, but you went too deep. Good thing you had an old man like me to watch you from ashore and occasionally drop the odd pearl.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: But the revenants didn't heed my call.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I half expected as much. Having spent so many years in the Furnace, their brains have been torched. No, they haven't had brains in a long time.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: You, the schemy kid. Yes, you. Give me a hand. Take the notepad from my coat's inside pocket, and a few pens, too.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You aren't going to suddenly wake up and grab my hand, right? Like that kind of thing in the horror stories.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I'm not that cliche. Once you have the notebook, write down whatever you want to say to the revenants, tear the pages out, and burn them.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: The lighter's in my pants pocket. Or use Arts. Either way.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Will that really reach them?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: They can't make me look bad, right?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Write down whatever you want, but I suggest topics they might be interested in—Hey, what do you folks want to know about?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Things about Kazdel. Write them down, tear the pages out, burn them.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: What are you doing right now...?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I ran into an old friend. We're catching up. Don't worry about me.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I'm finished! Ermi, make me a fireball, will you?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Can't you manage simple Arts like that...? Never mind. Who else has something ready to burn?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: No need. I found the lighter.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Nymph, what did you write?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Not telling. Wishes don't come true if you say them out loud.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You aren't making a wish!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Can you feel it? The Furnace seems to be shaking... I can see it!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: The ancestors have manifested!

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Me? Actually, he came to me back then too, but I didn't go with him.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I saw the bones on him, clattering away. Were you in there?

a.text: Memories don't do anyone any good here other than... adding to the suffering.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: But you still recognized me.

a.text: Because I loathe you. We loathe you.
Our resentment fanned the flames... It's what he wished.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: You lot certainly have a reason to loathe. I find myself with hard feelings every now and then, too.

a.text: You should never have returned. Why are you here?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Let's just say I'm here to see old friends. I've spent too much time in Columbia, waking up every morning to see a bunch of newly invented gadgets. But sometimes, I reminisce on old times and old friends.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: That's why I decided to take a vacation and came back here. It's been centuries, and I heard Kazdel got rebuilt again. I was curious what the place would look like.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I heard that they'd be renovating this Furnace soon and there would be a celebration to release all of you. Haha, though I wonder if you'll last that long.

a.text: It's more of a... funeral. An endless funeral.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I'm aware.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Revenants. All of you died long ago, but you need a funeral nonetheless.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I understand that. I do...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: In some parts of Columbia, you tell jokes about the dead at funerals. Everybody laughs and forgets the teary parts. I think that's a pretty good tradition. More places should have funerals like that.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I just so happened to have met some interesting kids, and they've got some interesting ideas. Why not hear what they have to say? Think of it as a rehearsal for your funeral.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Try not to scare them, though. They... They're all good Kazdelian kids.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: It's only been a second. Why are my legs so stiff? Seems I need to find some time for a spa treatment on my joints.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Hm? Where's my lighter?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: The schemy boy took it.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Can you feel it? The Furnace seems to be shaking... I can see it!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: The ancestors have manifested!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Nymph! Watch out! Come over here.

a.text: You think you have the right to stand before the revenants and talk about the future of Kazdel?

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: Not only the future... What I wrote is probably more like legends and folktales?

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: Those mercenaries sounded pretty confident, and I wasn't sure if it was true, so I figured I would ask you if there was ever really a Kazdel city that fell straight to the ground, leaving only a big pit?

a.text: You would curse Kazdel to be buried in the earth over a mere squabble?

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: Curse? Perish the thought. If such a place actually exists, I want to see it. I might just find some lost treasures I could use to expand my style.

steps.name: Crownie
steps.text: I've already thought up the exhibition's title. 'The Lost Kazdel: Echoes of Eras Past'. Sounds classy, don't you think?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: There's been so many Kazdels over the course of history. Maybe one of them really did come crashing down...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Uh, I'm just running my mouth. Don't get mad at me.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: What I wrote is my hopes for Kazdel's future, nothing too wild.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Really? Let's see... 'In a New Kazdel, the Sarkaz help one another, and outsiders no longer have to crowd on the city outskirts.'

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: 'People come here for better lives regardless of race, and there is no Royal Court anymore.' Pohl, did you write that?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Th-That's mine! Didn't I burn it? How did you find it?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Regardless of race... No Royal Court...

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Can you see what I wrote?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Yes. Well... Your vision is pretty bold, Gargoyle. I'm afraid it may never come true.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: A lot of people said the same thing a lot of years ago, to another Gargoyle.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: (Whispers) Ermi, Ermi. Which step of the ceremony are we on?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: We're not on any step. Ever since the ancestors showed up, I've completely lost control of this ceremony.

spans.text: step. Ever since the ancestors showed up, I've completely lost control of this ceremony.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Right now, the feeling I'm getting is that the ancestors are toying with us.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Toying?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: They seem to enjoy hearing a different kind of stories.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Crashing to the earth, flying into the sky, no Royal Court, and an entire city turned to revenants... You people come up with some wild ideas. Do you really think—

a.text: Do you really think that, compared to the way it is now, Kazdel would be better like that?
If Kazdel makes its way toward one of them, only to find it's the wrong path, what will you do?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: There's no such thing as 'the wrong path'.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Nobody knows what form Kazdel will ultimately take, but all of us want the people here to live better lives.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: If life gets better, how could you call it the wrong path?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Even if the path we end up taking is a treacherous one, it would be better than finding ourselves at a dead end, wouldn't it?
There is no response from the furnace core. The Tin Man looks down once again, all while his finger continues to rhythmically tap his other arm.
Nymph feels her heart beating faster, as the staff in her hand gets hotter.
Come on, hurry up and say something. Nymph glances at Crownie to plead for help, but she sees only a dark shadow in the distance.

a.text: If you think Kazdel would be better that way, then try it for yourselves.
You will prove for yourselves whether the outcome is good or bad, and you will bear any consequences.
Let's see if you truly have the right to find Kazdel... a different path.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: A different path... to where?

a.text: To the stories you just told.
